_Supersedes #29706 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Make manual single-issue dispatch retain live worker ownership while provider selection, canary validation, and worker preparation complete. Derive the default readiness budget from the canary timeout plus a bounded preparation allowance.

## Why

A v3.32.232 smoke dispatch selected `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, passed canary, and reached `post_worker_prepare`. `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` allowed only 20 seconds for provider selection, canary, and preparation, then restored `status:available` and removed the assignee. The still-running child consequently failed its ownership fence with `WORKER_OWNERSHIP_LOST`.

Timeline evidence shows the same actor assigned the issue at 05:32:29Z, queued it at 05:32:32Z, and unassigned it at 05:33:17Z. `headless-runtime-lib.sh` permits default canary validation for 180 seconds, so the 20-second readiness limit can revoke a live worker before it reaches `worker_started`.

## How

- Modify `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` to derive the default manual-dispatch readiness budget from `CANARY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` in `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh` plus a bounded preparation allowance.
- Preserve the explicit `AIDEVOPS_DSI_READY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` override, including zero for tests, and fall back safely for invalid readiness or canary timeout values.
- Preserve early detection of a dead detached child and the fail-closed issue ownership fence. Do not weaken the runtime ownership fence.
- Add or update focused coverage in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`.

Reproduce with `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh dispatch <issue-number> <owner/repo>`: let provider selection, canary validation, and preparation exceed 20 seconds while the detached child remains alive. The parent must not restore `status:available` or remove the assignee before `worker_started`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Default readiness cannot expire before the default canary budget.
- [ ] Explicit readiness overrides remain deterministic, including zero for tests.
- [ ] Invalid canary and readiness timeout values fall back safely.
- [ ] A live slow-starting worker is not self-revoked at 20 seconds.
- [ ] Existing dead-child and no-marker failure tests remain green.
- [ ] Bash 3.2 compatibility, dedup ceremony, bounded waits, and fail-closed ownership behavior are preserved.

body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->
# Keep unrelated global tool upgrades out of aidevops update

## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `aidevops update unrelated global tools report-only update-tools compatibility pin implementation issue full-loop` returned 0 hits — no relevant stored lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 9 recent commits / 6 historical merged PR search results / 0 open PRs touched or referenced the target surface; recent commits changed release metadata or other update paths, and no in-flight collision changes `_update_check_tools`
- [x] File refs verified: 6 refs checked against current `origin/main` (`3015614e8`); all existing paths are present and the proposed test parent is tracked
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — behavior is decided, but a focused shell regression harness still requires implementation judgment
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — the interactive implementation will create the normal draft PR after focused tests pass

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-08-07
- **Session:** OpenCode:current interactive session
- **Created by:** AI DevOps (ai-interactive)
- **Parent task:** none; leaf issue
- **Blocked by:** none
- **Conversation context:** The user clarified that `aidevops update` should update the framework and required compatibility dependencies only. Unrelated global tools may be reported, but mutation must require the separate explicit tool-update workflow.

## What

Keep the quick key-tool freshness report in `aidevops update`, classify OpenCode against its approved compatibility pin, and remove the prompt plus every path that invokes the mutating `tool-version-check.sh --update` command. Direct `aidevops update-tools --update` remains the explicit compatibility-aware mutation route.

## Why

PR #2161 intentionally added a prompt that can turn a framework update into broad global-tool mutation. That couples unrelated package-manager changes to the default update path, surprises interactive users, and is unsuitable for headless execution. The report remains useful; authority to mutate unrelated global tools must be explicit.

## Reproducer

- **Symptom command**: Run `aidevops update` while OpenCode or GitHub CLI is stale, then answer yes to `Run full tool update check? [y/N]`.
- **Actual output**: `_update_check_tools` reports the stale tool, reads the answer, and executes `bash "$tool_check_script" --update` from `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-update-lib.sh:332-333`.
- **Production entry point**: `aidevops.sh:457` calls `_update_check_tools` during every default framework update.
- **Call chain**: `cmd_update` calls `_update_check_tools`, which calls `tool-version-check.sh --update`, which runs package-manager update commands for all detected outdated tools.
- **Integrated verification**: Current `origin/main` source and merged PR #2161 both show the prompt-to-mutation path; no live installer was executed while filing this safety fix.
- **Causal status**: confirmed from the owning production call path and source-level mutation branch.

## Tier

### Tier checklist (verify before assigning)

- [ ] **Exact execution contract supplied?** The behavior boundary is exact, but the test harness implementation is not a verbatim replacement.
- [x] **Targets and reference pattern verified?** Current caller, mutation line, explicit command, and pin tests are identified.
- [x] **No semantic or design decision remains?** Reporting versus mutation behavior is decided.
- [x] **Bounded, reversible, low-consequence impact?** The change removes mutation from one update path and is reverted by restoring one branch.
- [x] **No stateful coordination to invent?** No persistent state or migration is added.
- [x] **Focused verification and rollback are explicit?** Focused shell tests and changed-file lint are listed below.
- [x] **No dispatch-path risk override?** The target is update behavior, not worker dispatch infrastructure.

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The trust boundary and compatibility policy are decided, while the focused Bash regression harness still needs normal implementation judgment.

## PR Conventions

This is a leaf issue. The implementation PR uses the normal closing keyword and a `GH#NNN:` title.

## Seeded Draft PR

- **Decision:** Skipped
- **Rationale:** Issue-only is sufficient; the active interactive session will implement and verify before opening the draft PR.
- **Status:** `not-created`
- **Freshness evidence:** memory, commit history, open and merged PR searches, and target-file verification completed against `origin/main` `3015614e8`
- **Verification run:** discovery only; implementation tests are not yet run
- **Stale-assumption warning:** re-check current `origin/main` and open PRs before editing; stop if `_update_check_tools` changed in flight

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-update-lib.sh:279-335` — retain report-only freshness checks and remove prompt-driven mutation
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-update-tool-reporting.sh` — prove compatibility-aware stale-tool reporting is non-interactive and non-mutating

Reference without modification:

- `aidevops.sh:450-458` — `cmd_update` caller
- `aidevops.sh:669-685` — explicit `update-tools` forwarding path
- `.agents/scripts/tool-version-check.sh:23-67` — `--update` opt-in parsing
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-version-check-opencode.sh:79-119` — compatibility-pin behavior that must remain green

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `aidevops.sh:457` calls `_update_check_tools`; `aidevops.sh:671-685` separately exposes `aidevops update-tools`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-update-lib.sh:332-333` reads interactive input and invokes `tool-version-check.sh --update`; direct and scheduled tool-update paths are separate and out of scope.
- **Tests/fixtures:** add the focused reporting test; retain `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-version-check-opencode.sh` for the OpenCode pin and package-manager routing.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A because exact searches found only shell callers and tests, with no schema or configuration consumer.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** setup deploys `.agents/scripts/` into the runtime bundle; no committed generated mirror needs editing.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because this report-only shell path has no persisted data, migration, or backfill surface.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-update-lib.sh` writes no state after this change; rollback is the inverse source diff.

### Implementation Steps

1. Preserve the current GitHub CLI minimum warning and quick version lookups, but classify OpenCode against `OPENCODE_PINNED_VERSION` when the pin is not `latest`, following the shipped `tool-version-check.sh` policy from GH#29311.
2. When stale tools are found, print the count and versions plus `aidevops update-tools --update` guidance; do not call `read`, prompt, or invoke the tool checker with `--update`.
3. Add a sandboxed regression test with stub commands that proves stale versions are reported and any attempted installer or mutating tool-check call fails the test.
4. Run the focused reporting test, the existing OpenCode compatibility test, ShellCheck, and changed-file lint.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** the report performs only command/version lookups; removing mutation eliminates package-manager write races from this path.
- **Migration/rollback:** no migration exists; source rollback restores prior prompt behavior without data conversion.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** output continues to identify stale key tools and the explicit command; matching `OPENCODE_PINNED_VERSION` is treated as current, real pin drift is reported against the approved version, and the GitHub CLI minimum warning remains unchanged.
- **Idempotency/retry:** repeated `aidevops update` runs only re-query versions and print guidance; they do not change global tools.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** failed registry lookups continue to be skipped, while explicit tool updates retain their existing command-specific failure handling.

### Complexity Impact

- **Target function:** `_update_check_tools` in `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-update-lib.sh`
- **Current line count:** 57 lines (threshold: 100 lines)
- **Estimated growth:** net reduction
- **Projected post-change:** below 57 lines
- **Action required:** none; keep the function simple and report-only

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-update-tool-reporting.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-version-check-opencode.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-update-lib.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-update-tool-reporting.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** the new test proves report-only default behavior; the OpenCode test proves compatibility pin and package-manager routing; ShellCheck and changed-file lint cover Bash quality and repository gates.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required because no shared config, dependency graph, generated schema, or cross-package contract changes.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused tests pass: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-update-tool-reporting.sh && bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-version-check-opencode.sh`
- [ ] WIP commit created before broader gates: `wip: separate tool reporting from updates`
- [ ] Evidence-triggered broad verification then run: `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-update-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-update-tool-reporting.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A stale OpenCode or GitHub CLI version is reported with installed and available versions and directs the user to `aidevops update-tools --update`.
- [ ] OpenCode at `OPENCODE_PINNED_VERSION` is not reported stale when the registry has a newer release; drift on either side of the pin is reported against the approved version.
- [ ] `aidevops update` never prompts for a full tool update and never invokes `tool-version-check.sh --update`, including with interactive stdin and headless execution.
- [ ] `aidevops update-tools --update` remains the explicit mutating route and continues to honor compatibility pins and installation-method routing.
- [ ] Failed or unavailable latest-version lookups remain non-fatal and do not trigger mutation.
- [ ] Focused tests, existing OpenCode compatibility tests, ShellCheck, and changed-file lint pass.

## Context & Decisions

- Keep the useful quick freshness report introduced by PR #2161.
- Separate observation from mutation: default framework updates report; explicit tool updates mutate.
- Apply the existing GH#29311 `OPENCODE_PINNED_VERSION` classification policy to the quick report while preserving the GitHub CLI minimum and install-method detection.
- Do not alter the independent idle/scheduled tool-freshness routine in this issue.
- Do not add a new flag or prompt to `aidevops update`; the existing explicit command is the authority boundary.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-update-lib.sh:279-335` — current report and prompt-driven mutation
- `aidevops.sh:450-458` — default update call site
- `aidevops.sh:669-685` — explicit update-tools command
- `.agents/scripts/tool-version-check.sh:23-67` — explicit `--update` parsing
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-version-check-opencode.sh:79-119` — compatibility-pin regression coverage

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** none
- **Blocks:** predictable non-interactive framework updates and safe separation of global-tool maintenance
- **External:** public package registries are stubbed for focused tests; no credentials or purchases are required

## Estimate Breakdown

| Phase | Time | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| Research/read | 15m | completed against current update paths and history |
| Implementation | 20m | report-only source change and focused test |
| Testing/review | 25m | focused tests, lint, PR review, and CI |
| **Total** | **1h** | bounded shell behavior change |

title: Headless close comments bypass signature and body-file guards
body:
## Task

Make headless/OpenCode GitHub-write enforcement cover closing comments supplied through `gh issue close --comment` (including `-c` and `--comment=`), so worker-authored closure comments cannot bypass the canonical body-file, signature, and audit path.

## Evidence

A real v3.32.232 smoke worker correctly determined that a managed private-repository issue was stale, then executed this raw write shape:

`gh issue close <issue-number> --repo <registered-private-repository> --comment '<closure evidence>'`

The command was allowed, closed the issue, and posted a bare comment without the canonical `<!-- aidevops:sig -->` footer. The worker stayed within its assigned issue, but bypassed the required wrapper and same-command body-file discipline.

The current code documents the gap:

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-signature.mjs:7-8` scopes signature enforcement to `gh issue create|comment` and `gh pr create|comment`.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-close-signature.sh:10-13` states that `issue:close --comment` is absent from the `gh` PATH-shim intercept list.
- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-close.sh:104-110` compensates only its own auto-close path by manually appending a signature.

No private repository name, issue number, title, or local path is required to reproduce or fix this framework gap.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**

`gh issue close <issue-number> --repo <owner/repository> --comment 'Resolved by PR #123. Verified against current HEAD.'`

**Actual output**

`✓ Closed issue <owner/repository>#<issue-number>`

The resulting closure comment lacks `<!-- aidevops:sig -->`, and the raw write does not pass through the canonical signed body-file wrapper.

1. Start a headless OpenCode worker on a maintained-repository issue whose verified outcome is “already fixed; close with pointer.”
2. Let the worker invoke `gh issue close ... --comment ...` directly.
3. Observe that the tool hook and PATH shim allow the command.
4. Inspect the posted comment and observe that it has no canonical signature footer.

Expected: a close command carrying comment content is either safely transformed/routed through the signed body-file path before closure, or blocked with exact wrapper/body-file recovery guidance. A close command without comment content should remain unaffected.

## Files

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-signature.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-signature-body-file.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-signature-footer-gate.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/gh-write-policy-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim-policy-cases.sh`
- Reference pattern: `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-close.sh` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-close-signature.sh`

## Implementation

- Detect `gh issue close` comment-bearing forms: `--comment VALUE`, `--comment=VALUE`, and `-c VALUE`, including commands in safe chains.
- Route comment content through canonical signature/body-file handling before any close side effect, or fail closed with an exact safe-command replacement.
- Preserve issue number/URL, `--repo`, `--reason`, and other close-only arguments.
- Ensure a retry cannot post the closing comment twice or perform ambiguous partial mutation.
- Keep comment-free `gh issue close` behavior unchanged.
- Prefer one enforcement source shared by interactive and headless OpenCode execution rather than another caller-specific manual signature workaround.

## Verification

- Add focused plugin tests covering all three comment flag forms, comment-free close, safe chained commands, and unparseable body syntax.
- Add/update PATH-shim or wrapper tests proving signed body-file routing and exactly-once close behavior.
- Run `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-signature-footer-gate.mjs`.
- Run the relevant `test-gh-shim-*` and wrapper test scripts.
- Run `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh`.

## Acceptance

- Raw `gh issue close --comment`, `--comment=`, and `-c` cannot publish an unsigned closure comment from OpenCode/headless workers.
- Safe handling preserves all close arguments and produces exactly one signed comment and one closure mutation.
- Unparseable or ambiguous command forms fail before the GitHub write.
- Comment-free issue closure remains supported.
- Existing issue-sync close behavior and signature tests remain green.
- Bash 3.2 compatibility and GitHub write audit logging are preserved.

## Hazards

Avoid double-posting when a comment succeeds but closure fails, and avoid silently changing `--reason` semantics. Keep private-repository identity out of public test fixtures and diagnostics. Do not weaken external-repository write guards, collaborator checks, or existing signature-footer enforcement.

## Goal
Prevent compromised or unexpectedly updated npm/Bun dependencies from entering aidevops installs and CI while retaining an actionable malware-response path.

## Evidence and implementation
The completed branch adds exact dependency pins, a committed Bun lockfile, frozen installs with lifecycle scripts disabled, delayed Dependabot updates, scheduled audit and malware/IOC scanning, and scanner regression coverage. The incident audit found no exact malicious package/version or persistence/hash matches on the scanned local repositories.

## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-08-07
- **Session:** OpenCode interactive release-closeout follow-up after #29712
- **Created by:** AI DevOps (ai-interactive)
- **Parent task:** none; independent leaf follow-up
- **Blocked by:** none
- **Conversation context:** Release provenance recovery showed that the `gh` PATH shim rewrote a squash-merge commit body after its terminal aggregation trailers, making Git's trailer parser return no provenance.

## What

Keep `gh pr merge --body` byte-for-byte unchanged by signature-footer injection. Continue intercepting `pr merge` for the headless external-write guard, privacy scanning, transport telemetry, and any safe-wrapper audit behavior; exempt only its merge-commit body from GitHub content-signature mutation.

## Why

For a squash merge, `gh pr merge --body` becomes the Git commit message. Git trailers are machine-readable only when they remain one contiguous terminal block. The shim currently appends `<!-- aidevops:sig -->` and attribution after that block, so release aggregation provenance disappears from `git interpret-trailers --parse` even though the visible trailer lines remain in the commit message.

Signature footers are required for issue, PR, review, and comment content. A merge commit body is a different semantic channel, and the OpenCode signature gate already excludes `gh pr merge`. Preserving the exact commit message is safer and narrower than attempting to parse and reposition arbitrary trailer-like prose.

## Reproducer

- **Symptom command**: `git show -s --format='%B' 4365863f8b7e0cabe30a62c39b92fba92e667408 | git interpret-trailers --parse`
- **Actual output**: `(no output)` even though the commit body visibly contains `Aidevops-Release-Aggregator-PR` and two `Aidevops-Release-Aggregates` lines.
- **Expected output**: the three aggregation trailers, unchanged and parseable as one terminal trailer block.
- **Production entry point**: `.agents/scripts/gh:243-259` routes `pr:merge` through the intercepted-write path; the generic body scanner and appender at `.agents/scripts/gh:836-936` then signs any `--body` value without considering the subcommand.
- **Call chain**: `gh pr merge ... --body "$merge_body"` enters the PATH shim, `_modified_args` retains `pr merge`, the `--body` scan appends `gh-signature-helper.sh footer`, privacy scanning runs, and native `gh` receives the rewritten commit body.
- **Integrated verification**: commit `4365863f8b7e0cabe30a62c39b92fba92e667408` from PR #29629 has the aggregation trailers followed by the injected signature and parses as empty. Corrective commit `a9ef2fc3316c0efea209c4c87816d81a450a2a80` places its signature before the terminal trailer block and the same parser returns all four expected aggregation trailers.
- **Causal status**: confirmed from the historical commit bodies, parser output, shim interception path, and signature appender.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The desired behavior is decided: do not sign `pr merge` bodies. Regression coverage must also prove that policy interception remains active and ordinary GitHub content writes continue to be signed.

## PR Conventions

This is a leaf issue. Use `GH#NNN:` in the PR title and `Resolves #NNN` in the PR body.

## Seeded Draft PR

- **Decision:** Skipped
- **Rationale:** The implementation boundary and historical reproducer are exact; normal worker implementation is sufficient.
- **Status:** `not-created`
- **Freshness evidence:** issue/PR collision checks and target verification completed against `origin/main` `abe6e48`, including merged PR #29716
- **Stale-assumption warning:** re-check `origin/main` before editing; stop if a newer change already introduces command-specific body-signing eligibility

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh:836-971` - bypass only signature mutation of `--body` and `--body=` when the command is `pr merge`; retain the rest of the intercepted-write pipeline
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim-core-cases.sh` - prove merge bodies and terminal trailers reach native `gh` unchanged while ordinary content writes remain signed
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim-routing-cases.sh:371-453` - prove headless external `pr merge` remains blocked and explicitly allowed or maintained-repository merges still reach transport

- `.agents/scripts/gh-write-policy-lib.sh:160-169` - `pr:merge` belongs in content-write policy interception and must remain there
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-signature-detection.mjs:64-82` - current content-signature contract covers PR create/comment and comment-bearing issue close, not PR merge
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh:491-507` - `gh_pr_merge_safe()` forwards to `gh pr merge` and does not request wrapper auto-signing

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** interactive sessions, full-loop helpers, and workers may invoke raw `gh pr merge` or `gh_pr_merge_safe`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** the PATH shim is the production mutation point; native `gh` writes the resulting squash/merge commit body to GitHub.
- **Tests/fixtures:** the hermetic shim harness records native argv; add a trailer-bearing merge body and policy-guard cases without contacting GitHub.
- **Schemas/config:** release aggregation consumes terminal `Aidevops-Release-*` Git trailers; their names and parser contract are unchanged.

- **Migrations/backfills:** none. Historical commit `4365863f...` remains immutable; later corrective aggregation already restored provenance.

3. Add hermetic `--body` and `--body=` cases containing a summary followed by two Git trailers. Assert that native argv contains no generated signature, preserves the exact body, and yields both trailers through `git interpret-trailers --parse`.
4. Add a policy regression proving an uninstigated headless merge to an external repository is still blocked before native transport. Preserve an allowed-path case.

- **Security boundary:** removing `pr:merge` from interception would weaken the headless external-write guard and is not acceptable.
- **Privacy boundary:** the exact merge body must still pass through `_shim_privacy_scan` before transport.
- **Attribution compatibility:** ordinary GitHub content writes and comment-bearing issue close commands must continue receiving canonical footers.
- **Commit semantics:** do not inject, move, normalize, or reflow merge commit body text; exact pass-through avoids trailer and signed-message regressions.
- **Shell compatibility:** retain Bash 3.2 support and explicit returns for any new shell function.

### Verification Before Dispatch

- The recommended fix is an exact `pr merge` signature exemption, not footer relocation. The OpenCode signature gate and original GH#20306 scope already treat merge commit bodies as outside the content-signature contract.
- `pr:merge` entered the broad intercepted-write case through t3598/GH#24719 for the external-write guard; it must stay intercepted even though its body must not be rewritten.

- **External:** none; regression verification must be hermetic and require no credentials or live merge

title: Pulse exhausts REST core quota while GraphQL-only breaker stays open
body:
Problem: Pulse can consume the authenticated maintainer's entire 5,000/hour REST core pool, blocking interactive reviews and cryptographic approvals. Evidence: a live incident recorded 90,097 attempted requests and 65,007 known REST-core points in 24 hours; the final hour consumed 4,850 known core points. After reset and Pulse restart, 287 known points were consumed in five minutes; pulse-merge-routine.sh accounted for 136 attempts and generic REST transport for 174. GET /user showed 356/5000 used while GET /rate_limit reported 3/5000 with a different reset epoch, so the current projection is not a reliable sole fuse for the active request principal. Deliverable: add a principal-consistent REST-core reserve that pauses all nonessential Pulse API-heavy stages, probes authoritative response headers when /rate_limit disagrees, caches probes, preserves quota for interactive maintainer work, recovers after reset, and prefers GitHub App installation auth when configured. title: Prioritize Pulse REST work and adapt the maintainer quota reserve
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `REST priority scheduler adaptive quota reserve` → 0 hits — no relevant stored lessons.
- [x] Discovery pass: 1 recent target-file commit / 0 related merged PRs / 0 open related PRs — #29737 is the shipped fixed-reserve baseline this task extends.
- [x] File refs verified: 6 target/config/test references checked, all present at HEAD `f9e68c486`.
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` — consequential dispatch-path scheduling and fail-open/fail-closed policy require cross-stage reasoning.
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — implementation should start only after the issue is claimed in this interactive full-loop session.

## What

Keep unattended Pulse work productive while preserving enough authenticated REST-core capacity for maintainer intervention. Replace the single all-or-nothing 500-request gate with stage-boundary priority classes and an adaptive soft reserve backed by a smaller emergency floor.

## Why

- The current fixed reserve protects 500 of 5,000 REST-core requests without a measured critical-demand model.
- The observed signed-maintainer approval flow for #29683 consumed roughly 18 known REST calls, while Pulse can consume hundreds of REST calls per five-minute window.
- Existing GraphQL scheduling already proves that stage-boundary deferral can preserve progress without introducing a stale durable request queue.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** This changes a self-hosting dispatch path and requires explicit quota-priority, recovery, and backward-compatibility decisions across multiple Pulse stages.

## Seeded Draft PR

- **Decision:** Skipped
- **Rationale:** Avoid anchoring implementation before the interactive issue claim and exact test design.
- **Status:** `not-created`
- **Freshness evidence:** Memory, collision, and target-file checks completed at `f9e68c486`.
- **Verification run:** Brief readiness only; implementation tests not yet run.
- **Stale-assumption warning:** Reassess if another open PR changes REST reserve or Pulse stage scheduling.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/configs/pulse-rate-limit.conf:47-61` — document adaptive soft reserve and hard floor defaults.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh:94-355` — classify authoritative REST headroom and gate progress work at the hard floor.
- `ADD: .agents/scripts/pulse-budget-priority.sh` — isolate GraphQL/REST stage classes and reusable priority-aware runners without growing the large wrapper.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:437-558` — source the scheduler and route deterministic stages through it.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1399-1490` — reuse the shared stage policy for costly prefetch work.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-routine.sh:278-288` — run merge progress until the hard floor rather than the soft optional-work reserve.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-graphql-budget-priority.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh`, and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-routine-standalone.sh` — encode threshold, priority-class, and orchestration regressions.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `pulse-wrapper.sh`, `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`, `pulse-merge-routine.sh`, and dispatch capacity checks calling `is_graphql_budget_sufficient`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** REST state is written only to the existing reset-aware cache by `pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh`; stage deferral writes existing Pulse logs/stats.
- **Tests/fixtures:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh` plus Pulse wrapper characterization/budget tests identified by `git ls-files` and exact search.
- **Schemas/config:** `.agents/configs/pulse-rate-limit.conf`; no serialized schema migration.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `~/.aidevops/agents/` is deployed only with `./setup.sh --non-interactive` after merge.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because no persistent queue or serialized schema is added; the existing `pulse-rest-core.json` cache remains compatible and missing config values use defaults.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_REST_CORE_RESERVE` and the new hard-floor override can collapse adaptive scheduling or restore fixed-reserve behavior; reset epochs automatically reopen deferred stages.

### Implementation Steps

1. Preserve authoritative ordinary-REST response headers and the existing short TTL/reset-aware cache.
2. Add `critical`, `progress`, and `deferrable` REST classes with a configurable 100-request hard floor. Compute the soft threshold by scaling the compatible 500-request cap toward the hard floor as reset approaches.
3. Generalise the existing GraphQL optional-stage wrapper. Deferrable enrichment, dashboards, broad sweeps, routines, and cache refreshes stop first; progress work continues until the hard floor; shared interactive wrappers remain ungated.
4. Route merge/dispatch/prefetch boundaries through the priority policy and reuse next-cycle retry, merge cursors, dispatch cooldowns, and cache refreshes instead of adding a durable request queue.
5. Add mode/stage deferral counters and focused tests, then perform a bounded production canary after merge/deployment.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Keep the existing credential-scoped, short-TTL cache and atomic write; concurrent stages may share observations but never a mutable request queue.
- **Migration/rollback:** New configuration has defaults and no migration ordering. Roll back by restoring the prior fixed reserve or setting soft cap equal to hard floor.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** Preserve `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_REST_CORE_RESERVE` as the soft-cap override and the existing `pulse_rest_core_reserve_allows` entrypoint.
- **Idempotency/retry:** Deferrals do not execute writes and retry through later Pulse cycles. Never replay queued writes.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** Unknown quota evidence conservatively defers optional/progress stages where safe; reset expiry invalidates stale evidence and restores normal scheduling automatically.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-graphql-budget-priority.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh

bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-canary.sh

.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** Circuit-breaker tests prove adaptive math and hard-floor gating; wrapper tests prove stage classes; ShellCheck proves Bash compatibility; changed lint covers integrated policy/config surfaces.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Run the full local linter only if changed lint reports shared-shell or generated-contract uncertainty.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [x] Focused tests pass: rate-limit breaker plus Pulse wrapper/dispatch/merge scheduling tests.
- [x] WIP commits created before broad gates: `157845a0a` and `538bbe534`.
- [ ] Evidence-triggered broad verification then run: `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`, broadening only when indicated.

### Safety-Stop Recovery

- **Original objective:** Keep unattended Pulse productive while preserving maintainer REST quota.
- **Preserved user directions:** Prioritize progress-critical requests before deferrable work and calibrate the oversized fixed reserve.
- **Trigger and evidence:** Not triggered.
- **Completed and verified:** None before implementation.
- **Remaining acceptance criteria:** All criteria below.
- **Unsafe route not to repeat:** Do not globally queue or block shared interactive GitHub wrappers.
- **Next safe route:** Narrow stage-boundary gating with existing retry/cursor mechanisms.
- **Resume condition:** Authoritative REST headers and focused test fixtures are available.
- **Owner and status:** Interactive full-loop session; not-triggered.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/configs/pulse-rate-limit.conf`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-budget-priority.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-routine.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-graphql-budget-priority.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-routine-standalone.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With healthy REST headroom, all three priority classes are eligible and existing Pulse behavior is unchanged.
- [ ] Below the adaptive soft reserve but above the hard floor, deferrable stages skip while progress-critical merge/dispatch work remains eligible.
- [ ] At or below the hard floor, new API-heavy progress work defers while critical maintainer/safety operations are not globally blocked.
- [ ] The adaptive threshold decreases monotonically toward the hard floor as reset approaches and never exceeds the configured soft cap or drops below the hard floor.
- [ ] Deferred work is retried by existing later-cycle mechanisms; no persistent request queue or delayed-write replay is introduced.
- [ ] Focused tests cover threshold boundaries, reset-time adaptation, unknown evidence, stage classification, and legacy override compatibility.

## Context & Decisions

- Prefer deterministic stage classes over a per-request queue because delayed reads become stale and delayed writes can violate preconditions.
- Keep 500 as a maximum early-window soft reserve, not an always-unavailable block; decay it toward a 100-request emergency floor as reset approaches.
- Existing next-cycle execution, cursors, and cooldowns own replay.

title: t18214: Make full-loop helpers use the sibling worktree gh shim
body:
## Task

Make full-loop helper execution deterministic: when `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` is invoked from a linked worktree, every nested `gh` call must resolve the sibling worktree `.agents/scripts/gh` shim rather than an older deployed shim that appears earlier on the inherited `PATH`.

## Why

Release aggregation exposed this during PRs #29744 and #29745. PR #29744 invoked the current worktree helper but a stale deployed shim appended a signature footer after terminal release-provenance trailers, invalidating the aggregation record. PR #29745 succeeded only after explicitly prepending the worktree scripts directory to `PATH`. Executing a helper from a worktree must select a coherent helper/shim version without manual environment repair.

## Tier

`tier:standard`: the affected boundary and likely pattern are known, but the implementation must preserve shell test stubs, installed-runtime behavior, idempotent PATH handling, and managed-shim recursion safety.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh:18-24` — establish deterministic sibling-shim resolution before sourced libraries execute nested `gh` calls.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh:77-1596` — affected nested call surface; prefer one orchestrator-level fix rather than editing every call site.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/` — add a hermetic regression test for worktree helper versus stale deployed shim precedence; retain the focused merge-body and native-resolution suites.

## Complete Write Surface

- Caller/reader: direct execution of `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`; sourced merge, state, risk, and commit libraries inherit its environment.
- Mutation path: `PATH` initialization in the orchestrator before sub-libraries run.
- Tests: a new focused resolution regression plus `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-body-file.sh` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim-native-resolution.sh`.
- Deployment mirror: `setup.sh` copies `.agents/scripts/` into the runtime bundle; do not edit deployed user-configuration copies.
- Schema, migrations, backfill, and persistent data: not applicable; this is process-local command resolution.
- Cleanup/rollback: revert the orchestrator PATH initialization and regression test.

## How

1. Derive behavior from the already resolved `SCRIPT_DIR` in `full-loop-helper.sh` and make the sibling scripts directory take precedence exactly once before any nested GitHub operation.
2. Preserve shell-function stubs used by tests and preserve execution outside a Git worktree.
3. Do not bypass the `gh` shim or point directly to a platform-specific native binary. The sibling shim must continue using its existing native-resolution logic.
4. Add a hermetic test with a deliberately stale shim earlier on inherited `PATH`, execute the worktree helper path, and prove the worktree shim handles the call.
5. Include a negative regression assertion that native `gh` resolution does not recurse through managed shims.

## Hazards and Compatibility

- Mixed-version safety: helper and shim must come from the same scripts directory for both repository worktrees and installed runtime bundles.
- Recursion: prepending the managed shim can loop unless the existing shim native-resolution exclusions remain intact; cover this explicitly.
- Idempotency: repeated sourcing/execution must not grow `PATH` with duplicate entries.
- Partial failure: if no sibling shim exists, retain a clear fallback or diagnostic rather than silently selecting an unrelated broken command.
- Concurrency and persistent-state ordering: not applicable; environment mutation is process-local.

## Verification Before Dispatch

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-body-file.sh` — exact merge-body transport remains intact.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim-native-resolution.sh` — managed-shim recursion/native lookup remains safe.
- Run the new hermetic worktree-versus-deployed-shim regression test.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh <new-or-changed-test-files>` — changed shell surfaces are clean.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Invoking the worktree `full-loop-helper.sh` with a stale deployed shim earlier on inherited `PATH` uses the sibling worktree shim for nested `gh` operations.
- Exact terminal release-provenance trailers are not followed by a footer injected by a stale shim.
- Existing installed-runtime behavior remains supported and native `gh` is reached without recursion.
- Repeated initialization does not duplicate the scripts-directory PATH entry.
- Focused tests pass and ShellCheck reports zero violations.

<!-- aidevops:generator=agent-doc-simplification-gate cited_file=.agents/reference/release-publication-controls.md threshold=500 -->

## Agent doc simplification (automated scan)

**File:** `.agents/reference/release-publication-controls.md`
**Detected topic:** Release Publication Controls
**Current size:** 500 lines

### Classify before acting

**First, determine the file type** — the correct action depends on whether this is an instruction doc or a reference corpus:

- **Instruction doc** (agent rules, workflows, decision trees, operational procedures): Tighten prose, reorder by importance, split if multiple concerns. Follow guidance below.
- **Reference corpus** (SKILL.md, domain knowledge base, textbook-style content with self-contained sections): Do NOT compress content. Instead, split into chapter files with a slim index. See `tools/code-review/code-simplifier.md` "Reference corpora" classification (GH#6432).

### For instruction docs — proposed action

Tighten and restructure this agent doc. Follow `tools/build-agent/build-agent.md` guidance. Key principles:

1. **Preserve all institutional knowledge** — every verbose rule exists because something broke without it. Do not remove task IDs, incident references, error statistics, or decision rationale. Compress prose, not knowledge.
2. **Order by importance** — most critical instructions first (primacy effect: LLMs weight earlier context more heavily). Security rules, core workflow, then edge cases.
3. **Split if needed** — if the file covers multiple distinct concerns, extract sub-docs with a parent index. Use progressive disclosure (pointers, not inline content).
4. **Use search patterns, not line numbers** — any `file:line_number` references to other files go stale on every edit. Use `rg "pattern"` or section heading references instead.

### For reference corpora — proposed action

1. **Extract each major section** into its own file (e.g., `01-introduction.md`, `02-fundamentals.md`)
2. **Replace the original with a slim index** (~100-200 lines) — table of contents with one-line descriptions and file pointers

title: Make Buzz OpenCode ACP compatibility release-independent
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Origin

Interactive full-loop request after Buzz Desktop 0.5.7 again launched managed OpenCode agents without the required `acp` argument. The user explicitly authorized implementation, merge, and an aidevops patch release.

## What

Replace the release-number allowlist in the Buzz Desktop compatibility helper with fail-closed structural drift detection, and add a dedicated idempotent OpenCode ACP wrapper that remains functional when Buzz clears `agent_args` during updates or restarts.

## Why

The existing helper supports only Buzz 0.5.4-0.5.5. Buzz 0.5.7 reproduced the same drift and required an emergency version override to restore three managed records. Frequent Buzz releases make per-version registry updates operationally brittle.

The startup defect is tracked upstream in `block/buzz` issue #3824. Upstream PR #4765 implements the preferred structural preset-argument resolution, but it remains open. The separately filed `block/buzz` issue #4891 concerns literal newline publication and does not fix ACP startup.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: `aidevops buzz reconcile`

**Actual output**: `Buzz Desktop 0.5.7 is not in the verified affected-version registry`, while `aidevops buzz status` reported `managed (0 OpenCode record(s))` and Fizz did not answer.

1. Install Buzz Desktop 0.5.7 with managed agents configured to launch OpenCode.
2. Confirm the managed records contain `agent_args: ["acp"]` and Fizz responds.
3. Update or restart Buzz until its synchronization rewrites those managed records to empty argument arrays.
4. Observe that Fizz launches bare OpenCode, does not complete ACP initialization, and stops responding.
5. Close Buzz and run the existing reconciliation with a 0.5.5 version override; three records are restored and Fizz returns online. Without the override, aidevops 3.32.234 refuses because 0.5.7 is absent from the version registry.

## Tier

`tier:thinking`: the change owns a private configuration mutation boundary, rollback behavior, mixed-version compatibility, and runtime command execution.

## Complete Write Surface

- `.agents/scripts/buzz-desktop-helper.sh`: remove release-number gating; validate structural eligibility; install/select the stable wrapper; reconcile only owned fields; preserve private backups, locking, atomic replacement, and rollback semantics.
- `.agents/bin/opencode-acp`: new idempotent shim that resolves the real OpenCode binary, injects `acp` only when absent, and fails closed instead of recursing.
- `.agents/tests/test-buzz-desktop-helper.sh`: cover unknown/future Buzz versions, empty args, wrapper drift, custom command/argument preservation, idempotency, rollback, malformed schema, symlinks, and running-app refusal.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-bin-shim-sync.sh` or equivalent deployment coverage: verify the new bin shim is deployed into `~/.aidevops/bin` without replacing unrelated user files.
- Callers/readers: `setup.sh` and `.agents/scripts/setup/_deployment.sh` already deploy `.agents/bin/*`; `aidevops.sh` routes `aidevops buzz` to the helper.
- Generated/deployed mirror: `~/.aidevops/agents/bin/opencode-acp` plus symlink `~/.aidevops/bin/opencode-acp`, created by the existing deployment path. Do not edit deployed copies directly.
- Migration/rollback: existing private state and backups must remain valid or migrate atomically; rollback restores only fields still matching aidevops-managed values.

## Hazards and Compatibility

- Concurrency: keep the existing lock and double-check that Buzz remains closed immediately before atomic store replacement.
- Security/privacy: validate owner, mode, regular-file/non-symlink constraints; never print store contents, keys, pubkeys, channels, or relay identities.
- Unknown schemas: fail closed before mutation. Future app versions are allowed only when the existing record structure and precise OpenCode command identity are recognized.
- User customization: preserve non-empty custom arguments and command overrides that do not exactly match aidevops-managed/original values.
- Idempotency: repeated apply/reconcile calls must not rewrite an already-correct store or duplicate `acp`.
- Mixed versions: the wrapper must accept either no arguments or a leading `acp`; it must not produce `opencode acp acp` after Buzz eventually ships its upstream fix.
- Partial failure: retain private bounded backups and restore the original store when state persistence or atomic replacement fails.

## How (Approach)

1. Deploy an `opencode-acp` bin shim through the existing `.agents/bin` mechanism. Resolve a non-self OpenCode executable, keep a leading `acp` unchanged, and otherwise prepend exactly one `acp`.
2. Replace `_buzz_is_affected_version` with structural compatibility checks over the validated store and known OpenCode command identities. Keep the app version only for diagnostics/state evidence.
3. Extend managed state so each owned record records the original command override and arguments plus the expected wrapper command. Migrate existing v1 state only when the live record still has a recognized original OpenCode command; otherwise fail closed.
4. During reconciliation, restore wrapper command/ACP arguments only for state-owned records whose current values are either the known original drift form or the exact aidevops-managed form. Preserve all other changes.
5. During rollback, restore only fields that still match aidevops-managed values; retain later user edits.
6. Keep locking, private backups, temporary files beside destinations, mode enforcement, and the final running-app recheck before atomic replacement.

### Files to Modify

- `NEW: .agents/bin/opencode-acp` — idempotent ACP launcher deployed through the existing bin-shim mechanism.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/buzz-desktop-helper.sh:77-525` — structural compatibility, state migration, wrapper ownership, reconciliation, status, and rollback.
- `EDIT: .agents/tests/test-buzz-desktop-helper.sh:97-391` — focused fixtures and regression coverage.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-bin-shim-sync.sh:88-125` — include the new owned shim in deployment verification if existing generic coverage does not already prove it.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `aidevops.sh` routes `aidevops buzz`; `.agents/scripts/setup/_deployment.sh` reads deployed `.agents/bin/*`; Buzz reads its managed-agent store and invokes the configured wrapper.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `.agents/scripts/buzz-desktop-helper.sh` is the only permitted writer for managed fields; `.agents/scripts/setup/_deployment.sh` creates the deployed wrapper symlink.
- **Tests/fixtures:** `.agents/tests/test-buzz-desktop-helper.sh` owns private-store fixtures; `.agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-bin-shim-sync.sh` owns deployment fixtures.
- **Schemas/config:** the helper validates Buzz record objects and owns `aidevops-buzz-opencode-acp-fix/v1`; implementation may introduce an atomically migrated v2 state schema.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** source `.agents/bin/opencode-acp` deploys to `~/.aidevops/agents/bin/opencode-acp` and links from `~/.aidevops/bin/opencode-acp` through `_sync_agent_bin_shims`.
- **Migrations/backfills:** `.agents/scripts/buzz-desktop-helper.sh` (`_buzz_validate_state`, `_buzz_write_apply_manifest`, and the new migration helper) migrates existing v1 private state only when live records still structurally match known OpenCode identities; no separate store backfill exists, and ambiguous records fail closed without mutation.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `_buzz_cleanup`, backup pruning, `cmd_rollback`, and bin-shim stale-link cleanup must retain current ownership boundaries.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add and directly test the non-recursive idempotent wrapper.
2. Replace version gating with validated structural eligibility and add state migration/ownership fields.
3. Update apply, reconcile, rollback, and status so only exact managed/original field states mutate.
4. Extend deployment and helper tests, then run focused checks and runtime double-restart verification.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** retain the lock, sibling temporary files, atomic rename, and immediately-before-write Buzz running check.
- **Migration/rollback:** atomically migrate recognized v1 state; rollback restores only exact aidevops-managed values and preserves later edits.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** structural validation supports newer Buzz releases while rejecting changed schemas; the wrapper accepts both bare and already-prefixed ACP invocations.
- **Idempotency/retry:** repeated wrapper calls inject one `acp`; repeated reconciliation does not rewrite correct stores or duplicate state.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** private bounded backup recovery remains mandatory when store/state writes fail; no partial state may claim ownership.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/tests/test-buzz-desktop-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-bin-shim-sync.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/buzz-desktop-helper.sh .agents/bin/opencode-acp .agents/tests/test-buzz-desktop-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** the helper test proves schema, mutation, migration, rollback, and negative-preservation boundaries; the bin-shim test proves deployment ownership; ShellCheck proves all changed shell surfaces; changed-file lint covers repository policy.
- **Broad verification trigger:** release publication and shared deployment behavior require the normal release/postflight gates after focused checks.
- **Broad verification command:** `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh`

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused tests pass: `bash .agents/tests/test-buzz-desktop-helper.sh`
- [ ] WIP commit created before broad gates: `wip: make Buzz ACP reconciliation release-independent`
- [ ] Evidence-triggered broad verification then run: `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh`

### Files Scope

- `.agents/bin/opencode-acp`
- `.agents/scripts/buzz-desktop-helper.sh`
- `.agents/tests/test-buzz-desktop-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-bin-shim-sync.sh`

## Verification Before Dispatch

- `bash .agents/tests/test-buzz-desktop-helper.sh` — focused mutation, drift, rollback, schema, and version-independent behavior.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-bin-shim-sync.sh` — deployment/shim ownership behavior if modified.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/buzz-desktop-helper.sh .agents/bin/opencode-acp .agents/tests/test-buzz-desktop-helper.sh` — shell correctness.
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh` — required repository quality gate after focused checks.
- Runtime: deploy from the reviewed worktree, close Buzz, reconcile, restart Buzz twice, verify three managed records remain functional, and confirm recent Fizz evidence shows `opencode acp`, relay connection, online presence, and no startup error without exposing private values.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Buzz 0.5.7 and a synthetic future version reconcile structurally without a version override when recognized OpenCode records drift to empty arguments.
- [ ] Unknown/malformed schemas, symlinked stores, running Buzz, unrelated commands, and custom arguments remain unchanged and fail/defer as appropriate.
- [ ] The wrapper injects exactly one `acp` when absent and preserves a leading `acp` plus remaining arguments.
- [ ] Existing managed state migrates safely or remains untouched; rollback restores only aidevops-owned fields and never overwrites later user edits.
- [ ] Deployment exposes the wrapper through the normal aidevops bin-shim path.
- [ ] A controlled double restart leaves Fizz launching through ACP and online.
- [ ] The implementation merges and publishes through the authorized aidevops patch-release workflow.

## Seeded Draft PR

Skipped. The implementation will begin only after this issue is created and claimed in a linked worktree.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/buzz-desktop-helper.sh:77-82` — brittle version allowlist.
- `.agents/scripts/buzz-desktop-helper.sh:110-172` — schema and target filtering.
- `.agents/scripts/buzz-desktop-helper.sh:219-341` — manifest and initial application.
- `.agents/scripts/buzz-desktop-helper.sh:344-525` — managed drift, rollback, status, and reconciliation.
- `.agents/tests/test-buzz-desktop-helper.sh:97-311` — fixtures and current bounded-version tests.
- `.agents/scripts/setup/_deployment.sh:6-51` — automatic `.agents/bin` shim deployment.

## Dependencies

- `jq`, already required by the helper.
- A locally installed OpenCode executable discoverable through the managed record or standard command lookup.
- No dependency on the upstream Buzz fix landing; when it does land, idempotent argument handling must remain safe.

title: bug: serialize parallel release lanes before publication and deployment
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `parallel release collision serialization lease setup deployment reconciliation` → no relevant lessons.
- [x] Discovery pass: 22 recent commits touched release targets; no related open PRs and no matching open issue found.
- [x] File refs verified at `ba19c1e92`: release entry, reconciliation, deployment gate, and setup mutex paths exist.
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` — cross-session coordination, stale-owner recovery, and publication safety are consequential state-machine decisions.
- [x] Seeded draft PR: skipped — implementation requires an explicit coordination design first.

## What

Add a repository-scoped release lane that prevents two interactive sessions from independently entering version bump, protected-main provenance, publication, reconciliation, or exact-tag deployment for aidevops at the same time. The lane must expose the active source PR/tag/phase and route later sessions to wait, reconcile, or aggregate rather than creating a competing release.

Also close the race where `main` advances after a signed release commit is prepared but before its provenance PR merges. Publication must fail before tag/package mutation when the merged descendant tree differs from the signed release tree, or the workflow must produce a newly reviewed exact-tip aggregation path. It must never publish a tag that cannot pass its own exact-tree deployment gate.

## Why

Two authorized sessions reached release/update stages concurrently during v3.32.236. While PR #29786 was being released, unrelated PRs merged into `main`, and another setup process deployed the descendant. The signed release commit `4867c5364` was later merged by PR #29790 into `ba19c1e92`, whose tree differed in four files. Publication succeeded, but reconciliation repeatedly failed with `active descendant ba19c1e92d4c: its tree differs from release 4867c53649de`. Setup lock waits and an audited exact-tag rollback/reconcile/restore sequence added substantial delay.

This is not only a setup mutex problem: `setup.sh` already serializes overlapping setup processes, but no repository-wide release ownership spans release preparation, protected-main merge, remote publication, postflight, and receipt finalization.

## Reproducer

1. Merge source PR A and start `aidevops release patch <PR-A> incremental` from session A.
2. Before its protected-main provenance PR merges and local receipt becomes terminal, merge unrelated source PR B from session B and run setup/deployment from current `main`.
3. Merge the release provenance PR without rebuilding its signed release commit. The resulting merge commit is a descendant of the release commit but has a different tree.
4. Let package publication converge, then run `aidevops release reconcile <PR-A>`.
5. Observe that public channels are published while post-release deployment rejects the active descendant because its tree differs from the signed release tree.

Observed with PR A `#29786`, provenance PR `#29790`, release `v3.32.236`, exact release commit `4867c5364`, and active descendant `ba19c1e92`. The expected behavior is to reserve one release lane and stop the incompatible second mutation before any irreversible tag or package publication.

## Evidence

- v3.32.236 tag commit: `4867c53649deb5ae2e517f3ce1fbc88ce0f5b820`, parent `1bde77c82`.
- Provenance merge: `ba19c1e92d4c109a6c45fe5e5786879ed36050fa`, with intervening `main` commits `e2f657716` and `21af3e9f9`.
- Tree difference affected `.agents/scripts/cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/init-routines-helper.sh`, and their tests.
- Publication run `31234510784` completed and all public channels converged before local deployment failed.
- `setup.sh` reported another owner and waited, proving setup serialization exists but begins too late to protect release provenance.
- Recovery required staging exact tag `4867c5364`, audited runtime rollback, `aidevops release reconcile 29786`, and restoration of current `main`.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Rationale:** This changes a release and deployment coordination boundary. The worker must decide durable lease scope, stale-owner recovery, aggregation behavior, and compatibility with remote continuation without weakening fail-closed provenance checks.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh` — acquire and inspect a repository-wide release lane before `_full_loop_release_run_new`; status remains read-only, while reconcile may adopt the matching lane.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh` — advance/release lane state only from verified tag, workflow, deployment, and terminal receipt evidence.
- `.agents/scripts/version-manager-release.sh` — keep exact-tree post-release verification fail closed; add pre-publication detection so an undeployable protected-main merge cannot reach channel mutation.
- `setup.sh` and/or the shared lock module it uses — make generic setup/deployment aware of an active exact-tag release deployment window without deadlocking normal setup.
- Pulse merge/release routing path, exact file to confirm during implementation — prevent a second release start and avoid merging an incompatible main change through an active release lane.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile.sh` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-auto-sync.sh` — extend existing release/reconciliation coverage.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-setup-noninteractive-lock.sh` or a new focused release-lane test — cover cross-process ownership, waits, stale recovery, and redacted diagnostics.
- `.agents/workflows/release.md` and `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md` — document lane behavior and recovery commands.

### Complete Write Surface

The worker must trace all call sites of `_full_loop_release_run_new`, `_full_loop_release_existing_command`, `run_post_release_agent_sync`, and the setup lock before editing. Keep lane state under the existing aidevops state root and key it by normalized repository slug, not worktree path or source PR alone. Include source PR, expected source set, phase, tag when known, owner/session metadata safe for diagnostics, heartbeat/update time, and terminal receipt linkage.

### Implementation Steps

1. Characterize two concurrent `aidevops release patch` invocations for different merged PRs. Assert only one can reserve the repository release lane and the loser receives the active PR/tag/phase plus the exact status/reconcile command.
2. Define a crash-safe lane lifecycle spanning local preparation, protected-main provenance, queued remote publication, reconciliation, exact-tag deployment, and terminal receipt. Process exit after queueing must not discard durable ownership; verified terminal evidence or bounded stale recovery must release it.
3. Make same-source status/reconcile idempotently adopt the lane. A different source must not bump a version while the lane is nonterminal; it should be queued for later aggregation or receive a deterministic retry path.
4. Revalidate `origin/main` immediately before protected release merge/tag publication. If the reviewed release commit would merge into a changed tree, stop before tag/package writes and require the existing exact-tip reviewed aggregation mechanism.
5. Coordinate exact-tag deployment and receipt persistence with generic setup so another session cannot replace the runtime between convergence verification and terminal receipt. Preserve the existing audited rollback path for genuine operator recovery.
6. Add stale-owner and interrupted-process tests. Never infer safety from PID absence alone when a remote workflow or immutable tag proves the release remains active.
7. Update release/full-loop documentation with operator-visible diagnostics and recovery.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- Do not hold a process-only lock while waiting for remote CI; release continuation is intentionally resumable from another trusted session.
- Do not weaken tag provenance, exact-tree runtime verification, setup rollback protection, or immutable-tag behavior.
- Do not block read-only `release status`. Same-release reconcile must remain recoverable after the initiating process exits.
- Prevent deadlock between release-lane and setup locks by documenting and testing one acquisition order.
- Redact command arguments and secrets from owner diagnostics, matching setup-lock tests.
- Multiple machines may share GitHub state but not local state; fail closed or use verified remote evidence when local ownership is insufficient.

### Verification Before Dispatch

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-auto-sync.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-setup-noninteractive-lock.sh`
- New focused test: parallel different-source releases result in one version mutation and one actionable blocked/reconcile result.
- New focused test: `main` advancing between release preparation and protected merge stops before tag or publication mutation.
- New focused test: interrupted queued publication remains adoptable by same-source reconcile and blocks a competing release.
- `shellcheck` on every changed shell file and `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Two parallel aidevops release sessions cannot create competing version bumps, provenance PRs, tags, or postflight deployments.
- A later session gets concise active-lane evidence and a deterministic wait/reconcile/aggregation action.
- A release whose protected-main merge tree differs from its signed release tree is stopped before public channel mutation.
- Remote queued publication remains resumable after process exit without stale local ownership blocking forever.
- Generic setup cannot invalidate the exact-tag deployment-to-receipt critical section.
- Existing successful single-release, same-source reconcile, setup mutex, and audited rollback behavior remains passing.

## Seeded Draft PR

- **Decision:** Skipped
- **Rationale:** The concurrency state machine and lock ordering need worker design and characterization before code is safely seeded.
- **Status:** `not-created`

title: Make solved attribution complete and measurable across completion paths
body:
## Problem

Completion attribution is incomplete and biased. For issues closed since 2026-08-01, only 98 of 298 likely completed issues had `solved:worker` or `solved:interactive`; sampled issues with verified merged PRs were missing attribution. Worker-origin coverage was materially higher than interactive-origin coverage, making comparative productivity analysis misleading.

## Reproducer

Run the completion-attribution report against closed issues since 2026-08-01. The observed baseline was 92 `solved:worker`, 5 `solved:interactive`, 0 conflicting, and 201 unattributed issues: 32.55% coverage. Inspecting unattributed completed issues shows merged closing PRs with explicit `origin:*` labels that existing closeout paths did not transfer to mutually exclusive `solved:*` labels.

## Goal

Apply mutually exclusive `solved:*` attribution consistently whenever a verified merged PR resolves an issue, regardless of whether Pulse, issue-sync, full-loop/native merge reconciliation, or task completion performs closeout. Add a guarded historical backfill and a coverage report/invariant.

## Implementation guidance

- Centralize actor derivation from the resolving merged PR labels in `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh`; do not infer solver from the issue `origin:*` label.
- Wire verified completion paths including `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-close.sh`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`, and task/full-loop reconciliation.
- Add or extend a dry-run-first backfill script that only labels completed issues with unambiguous linked merged-PR evidence; skip ambiguous, duplicate, and not-planned closures.
- Extend `worker-activity-helper.sh` or a focused helper to report attributed, unattributed, conflicting, and coverage percentage without presenting partial counts as complete.
- Preserve mutual exclusion and avoid applying `solved:*` to merely closed/unmerged PRs.

## Verification

- ShellCheck changed shell files with zero violations.
- Extend targeted regression tests for worker, interactive, native-auto-close/issue-sync, ambiguous evidence, mutual exclusion, dry-run backfill, and coverage calculation.
- Run `.agents/scripts/tests/test-solved-label-attribution.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-activity-helper.sh`, and relevant issue-sync/full-loop tests.
- Verify a sample fixture with an `origin:interactive` issue solved by an `origin:worker` PR is labelled `solved:worker`.

title: Implement and document compact worktree archive and restore commands
body:
## Task
Implement compact worktree archive/restore commands and documentation. Do not wire them into pulse/worker cleanup yet except for documenting the intended future integration points.

## Why
Disk pressure was caused by full recovery worktrees accumulating under ~/.aidevops/recovery/worktrees. Worker worktrees should be disposable runtime cache, while GitHub branches/PRs plus compact archives should be durable state.

## Commands to implement and document
Add .agents/scripts/worktree-archive-helper.sh with:
- archive <worktree-path> --repo owner/repo --issue N --reason failed-worker|post-pr-cleanup --base-branch <branch> [--base-sha <sha>] [--output-root <dir>]
- restore <archive-dir> --target <new-worktree-path>
- list [--repo owner/repo] [--issue N]
- verify <archive-dir>
- prune --older-than 14d --max-total-size 20G [--dry-run|--apply]
- optional: archive-current and restore-latest

## Archive contract
Store compact artifacts under ~/.aidevops/recovery/archives/<repo>/<issue>/<timestamp>/: manifest.json, commits.bundle when local commits exist, diff.patch, staged.patch if needed, untracked-files.txt, bounded untracked.tar.zst or .tar.gz, and failure.log/failure excerpt when available. Manifest must include repo, issue, reason, created_at, source worktree path, branch, head_sha, base_branch, base_sha, default_branch, remote branch state, dirty state, artifact list, and restore instructions. Base is not always main: prefer PR baseRefName, then dispatch metadata target branch, then repo integration/default branch; store exact base_sha.

## Documentation requirement
Document all commands, options, archive layout, restore workflow, base branch/base SHA selection, retention policy, and future pulse/worker flow. Put docs near the helper and link from worktree cleanup docs. State explicitly that pulse/worker integration is a follow-up after the helper is verified.

## Future integration notes to document only
After this helper lands, pulse can archive-before-delete terminal failed worker worktrees without PRs, delete clean pushed PR worktrees as disposable cache, and prune recovery archives/full recovery worktrees by retention and size caps. Preserve full worktrees only for interactive/manual owners, security incidents, preserve-forensics marker/label, repeated unexplained failures, or archive safety failures.

## Reference files
- .agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh
- .agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/worktree-clean-lib.sh
- .agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/dirty-worktree-backup-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/commands/worktree-cleanup.md
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-cleanup-*
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-*

## Acceptance
- Helper implements archive, restore, list, verify, prune, and help text with safe argument validation.
- Archive preserves local commits via bundle, dirty changes via patch, untracked files via bounded archive/list, and exact base metadata.
- Restore creates a fresh worktree from an archive and recovers commits/diffs/untracked files.
- Documentation covers every command and explicitly marks pulse/worker integration as a follow-up.
- Tests cover clean archive, local commits, dirty/untracked archive, restore from bundle+patch, verify, prune dry-run/apply, and invalid arguments.
- ShellCheck clean and targeted shell tests pass.

title: Recover stale ownerless full-loop cleanup receipt locks
body:
## Problem

An old empty `.mutation.lock.d` under the full-loop cleanup receipt state directory permanently blocks receipt writes. The lock acquisition loop only recovers locks with a dead numeric owner PID; an ownerless directory survives every retry.

## Reproducer

During PR #29804 cleanup, merge-time receipt recording, `adopt-merged-receipt`, and `full-loop-helper.sh complete` all failed. The lock directory was empty and approximately 7.5 hours old. Removing only that verified-empty stale lock allowed `complete` to write the receipt and targeted cleanup to reach `CLEANED`.

**Symptom command:** `full-loop-helper.sh complete`

**Actual output:** `Cannot persist durable deferred-cleanup handoff`

## Goal

Recover stale ownerless receipt locks without racing a process between lock-directory creation and owner-file publication.

## Implementation guidance

- Modify `.agents/scripts/full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`, especially `_full_loop_receipt_lock_acquire`.
- Preserve the existing numeric-owner dead-process recovery.
- Add a conservative age threshold and revalidation for empty/ownerless locks before removal; fail closed for fresh or malformed ownership evidence.
- Keep recovery scoped to the exact receipt lock directory and preserve transaction recovery semantics.

## Verification

- Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh` with fresh-empty, stale-empty, live-owner, dead-owner, and concurrent owner-publication fixtures.
- Run ShellCheck and the cleanup receipt/full-loop merge cleanup suites.
- Verify stale ownerless recovery creates a valid receipt while fresh ownerless locks remain untouched.

title: Fix worker Bun PATH and aidevops JS dependency bootstrap for existing installs
body:
## Task

Fix worker/pulse runtime handling so existing aidevops installations with Bun at `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun` can bootstrap aidevops JavaScript dev dependencies in worker worktrees without requiring a reinstall or shell startup files.

## Why

Observed on issue #29803: aidevops declares `typescript` in `package.json` and `typecheck` runs `tsc --noEmit`, but the worker-created worktree lacked `node_modules/.bin/tsc`. The worker then reached pre-push repo verification and failed with `tsc: command not found` and `typecheck could not start: missing JavaScript dev dependencies`. Manual recovery in the same linked worktree proved the dependency set is valid: `/home/alexey/.bun/bin/bun install` and `/home/alexey/.bun/bin/bun run typecheck` passed, then PR creation succeeded at #29808.

Root cause: worker/systemd/pulse paths do not reliably expose existing user tool installs such as `$HOME/.bun/bin`; the worktree bootstrap depends on `command -v bun`; pulse fallback restore intentionally skips root `node_modules`.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh` around `_bootstrap_aidevops_worktree_js_deps` lines 422-449. Add a Bun resolver that uses `command -v bun` first, then fixed existing install path `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun` when executable. Invoke the resolved binary directly for `install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` around `_dlw_append_node_tool_env` lines 1514-1522 and worker command assembly lines 1593-1622. Ensure worker commands get a runtime PATH prefix for existing user tool dirs: `$HOME/.bun/bin`, `$HOME/.local/bin`, `$HOME/.aidevops/bin`, and `$HOME/.aidevops/agents/scripts`, preserving repo `node_modules/.bin` precedence. Guard existing dirs, reject colon/newline, dedupe.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh` around `aidevops_launchd_sanitized_path` lines 444-450. Include `$HOME/.bun/bin` in stable scheduler PATH when the directory exists.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers.sh` fallback path around lines 37-45 if needed so behaviour is consistent when `shared-constants.sh` is not sourced.
- EDIT/ADD focused tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Existing installations with Bun only at `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun` bootstrap aidevops worker worktree JS deps without requiring shell rc files, reinstall, or `aidevops update` first.
- [ ] `_bootstrap_aidevops_worktree_js_deps` still does not run implicit package installs for non-aidevops projects.
- [ ] Worker launch PATH includes existing Bun/user tool directories while preserving repo `node_modules/.bin` precedence.
- [ ] Scheduler sanitized PATH includes `$HOME/.bun/bin` when present.
- [ ] Root `node_modules` restore remains disabled by default for pulse; do not solve this by globally enabling `WORKTREE_NODE_MODULES_RESTORE_ROOT_ENABLED=1`.

## Verification
